triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded none of HTS 9903.05.71's operative content — the country/column-1-below-12.5% condition, the 9903.05.85–9903.05.92 exception, and the 12.5% floor rates for columns (1-General) and (1-Special) were all parked as deferred_outputs, so the heading's floor rule and its exception clause were unrepresented in the module.
triage.triage_notes: This is the only substantive module change in chunk 4; indices 36-46 are the en-dash provenance sweep. Pre-fix the file held only two orphan parameters (threshold 0.125, floor rate 0.125) plus three deferred_outputs entries (name collision with the sibling .70 export and 'flattened thresholded/capped mechanics'); post-fix it exports a renamed floor_heading_applies plus general/special rate rules. Borderline call flagged for the reviewer: the gap was explicitly declared via deferred_outputs rather than silently mis-encoded, and the parent composition (us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml, index 0) already cited us/statute/hts/9903.05.71 directly in its own proof atoms, so no wrong number was being computed end-to-end — under the 'adds outputs the module never claimed' carve-out a reviewer could downgrade this to unclear. I kept it as fidelity/unrepresented_clause because the missing content is the heading's entire operative clause and the commit treats it as one of five review blockers. Provision read through the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union): HTS 9903.05.71 = 'Except for products described in headings 9903.05.85–9903.05.92, articles the product of South Korea, with an ad valorem ... rate of duty under column 1 less than 12.5 percent ... Rates of duty (1-General): 12.5% / (1-Special): 12.5% / (2): No change', which matches the new '<' boundary, the 0.125 floor and the 'No change' column-2 silence. The fix also widened source_verification to corpus_citation_paths [9903.05.71, 9903.05.70] and grounds the else-branch (rate unchanged) on the .70 complement — defensible cross-grounding, but note it is a second provision now cited by this module. A new companion test forced-labor-south-korea-9903-05-71.test.yaml adds the at-threshold boundary case (0.125 -> not_holds) and the exception case.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module encoded exactly two parameters (threshold 0.125 and floor rate 0.125), both of which match HTS 9903.05.71 ("less than 12.5 percent", "Rates of duty (1-General): 12.5%") and are carried into the post-fix file unchanged in value, dtype, and effective_from — nothing the module asserted disagreed with the source. The country condition, the 12.5% floor branch, and the 9903.05.85–9903.05.92 exception were not silently omitted: the module carried an explicit `deferred_outputs` block naming those three outputs, and the stated reason is a RuleSpec naming collision ("used a local name that collides with a sibling RuleSpec export"), i.e. a tooling/export-hygiene deferral, not a misreading of the provision. The pre-fix composition already computed the Korea floor top-up from these parameters (`elif origin_is_japan or origin_is_korea or origin_is_switzerland: (if mfn_ad_valorem_rate < forced_labor_section_301_twelve_and_one_half_percent_rate: ...`), so the deferral produced no wrong duty downstream. Per the rubric, adding outputs the module explicitly never claimed is new coverage, not a fidelity correction, so unrepresented_clause is not supported for this file.

triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence checked: pinned-release text of us/statute/hts/9903.05.71 (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision line 1344) reads "Except for products described in headings 9903.05.85–9903.05.92, articles the product of South Korea, with an ad valorem (or ad valorem equivalent) rate of duty under column 1 less than 12.5 percent, as provided for in U.S. note 52 to this subchapter / Rates of duty (1-General): 12.5% / Rates of duty (1-Special): 12.5%". The new formula uses strict `<` against the 0.125 threshold, matching "less than", so there is no boundary_direction issue either way.

What actually changed in module 47: (a) three previously deferred outputs are now encoded (heading_applies + general/special rate overlays); (b) both surviving parameters were renamed (south_korea_section_301_column_1_duty_rate_threshold -> forced_labor_south_korea_floor_column_1_rate_threshold; south_korea_section_301_floor_duty_rate -> forced_labor_south_korea_floor_duty_rate) with identical formulas '0.125' and identical effective_from '2026-07-24'; (c) provenance-only edits — hyphen to en-dash in the heading range, "as provided for in U.S. note 52 to this subchapter" added to the summary, and corpus_citation_path -> corpus_citation_paths with 9903.05.70 added for the else-branch grounding. No pre-existing formula, parameter value, version window, date, or scope was corrected.

Residual uncertainty (why 0.66 and not higher): if the reviewer's convention is that a heading module MUST export its own operative rate rule, then the deferral is itself the defect and unrepresented_clause could be defended. I weight against that because the deferral was declared in-file with a naming-collision reason and the operative floor logic was already live in us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml.

Reviewer pointer: the genuine fidelity content of commit 65997b4e49 (the 9903.05.85 in-transit safe harbor, note 52(g)/(h) USMCA exception, note 52(a) chapter-98 exclusion, personal-use baggage) lands in module index 0, us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml (321 diff lines) — that is where an unrepresented_clause claim for this commit should be adjudicated, not in this overlay file. A companion test file forced-labor-south-korea-9903-05-71.test.yaml was added alongside, consistent with new coverage rather than a corrected computation.
